facts.text: Find the treasure shown on the party's map.
facts.classification_change_basis: The party's established choices now centre on the dragon and the trip to the Barrow for Brandon's sword (beats 79-81). The treasure is checked only incidentally on the way (beat_81), so it is no longer the primary adventure.

facts.text: Where are the locations marked on the party's treasure map, and at which one does the treasure lie?

classification.question_basis: Beat_1 establishes the party follows a map whose marked locations they do not recognize in land unknown to them; identifying them is what the party must discover to find the treasure.
classification.grounding_justification: The fiction explicitly states the marked locations are unrecognized and the land unknown.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering it is mainly identifying places, though it may require piecing together local knowledge.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: The answer is mainly instrumental toward the treasure.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Locating unfamiliar map sites naturally supports asking locals, exploring and following leads.

facts.text: The party holds a treasure map with several marked locations, one of which they assume holds the treasure.

classification.support_basis: The map is the party's only guide to the treasure, though its locations are not yet recognized.

facts.text: The party plans to check one of the map's marked locations on the walk to the Barrow.

classification.opening_basis: The trigger is searching a marked location en route; the benefit is simply finding out whether the treasure is there, which is pursuing the want itself rather than gaining an advantage toward it.
classification.support_basis: It would test one candidate site for the treasure, but nothing establishes that this location holds it.
classification.action_basis: The party decided to walk to the Barrow and check a marked location on the way (beat_81).

facts.text: Where did the party's treasure map come from?

classification.question_basis: Beat_3 notes that Dr. Uriah, who carries the map, can recall nothing of its history; this is a gap about the map's origin with no anomaly beyond that, so it is ordinary.
classification.grounding_justification: Play states that the map's history is unknown even to its carrier, but does not frame it as a mystery.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Learning the map's origin could reveal who made it, but nothing suggests a concealed situation.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: The answer might be mildly interesting but is mainly background.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: No leads or sources on its history are established.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
facts.uncertain_reason: The party is now pursuing the dragon, but George doubts Eric actually has the 1000 gold (beat_58).
facts.classification_change_basis: Earlier the party had not taken up the hunt. This Session Uriah admitted he was offered money to go after the dragon (beat_46), Phidipaldi questioned George about it and vowed to bring his lance (beat_61), and the party shared dragon intelligence and set out for the Barrow to get the sword needed to kill it (beat_79, beat_81). The dragon hunt now drives the party's choices, so its priority changes from other to primary.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter in chain mail with a shield, offers to join the party for pay to hunt the dragon; she won't go alone.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hire Lady Hilda for an unstated fee. Benefit: an experienced armoured fighter added to the dragon hunt, reducing its risk.
classification.support_basis: A seasoned fighter adds real combat strength against a dragon that has already maimed a capable woodsman.
classification.action_basis: Hilda explicitly offered to join a party of adventurers for money, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would come back for her services.

facts.text: George, the one-armed woodsman who survived the black dragon, says it is not a big one, its poison-dripping jaws kill with one bite, and it spits sulfur that smells of rotten eggs.

classification.support_basis: First-hand knowledge of the dragon's lethal bite and sulfur spit lets the party prepare and avoid the mistakes that killed George's friends.

facts.text: Where did this new dragon come from, when Sir Brandon's dragon was killed centuries ago and none has appeared since?

classification.question_basis: Bentley and Gill stress nothing like this has happened since Sir Brandon killed the first dragon centuries ago; George repeats that only Brandon ever killed the dragon, 1000 or 2000 years ago, and that it cannot fly yet. This is an anomaly worth explaining in itself.
classification.grounding_justification: Several sources make the dragon's sudden appearance after centuries conspicuous, and none knows its origin.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden cause behind the dragon's return.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Explaining the dragon's return could reshape understanding of the town's legend and current troubles.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The legend, George, Gill's fairytales, the Barrow and the lair offer leads to follow.

facts.text: Where does the black dragon lurk outside Brandonsford?
facts.ended_how: answered: George says the lair is up north at the foot of the mountains (beat_56); replaced by fact_new_1

classification.question_basis: The dragon was only placed 'outside town'; finding it is required to kill it for the Reeve's bounty.
classification.grounding_justification: Sightings were reported but no location given.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: George, Gill and his sons were leads that could be questioned or followed.

facts.text: The black dragon killed George's friends at its lair and cost him his arm, and Gill's three sons are hunting it now. George says it cannot fly yet but soon will, and then the town is doomed.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The dragon has already killed a hunting party, Gill's sons are actively confronting it, and George names the town as doomed once it flies.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Death of hunters and potentially the whole town.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George is a first-hand survivor reporting deaths and his own injury; the flying claim is his prediction.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: George describes an advancing process: it cannot fly yet but soon will; the sons are hunting it now.
classification.preventability_justification: The party knows where the lair is and is seeking the sword said to kill it, though success is uncertain.

facts.text: George says the dragon's lair is up north at the foot of the mountains, with no climbing needed.

classification.support_basis: Tells the party where to find the dragon they must kill, from a survivor who went there.

facts.text: George says nothing pierces the dragon's black scales; his friends' arrows and swords all failed.

classification.scope_basis: The scales are a standing property of the dragon that defeated a whole hunting party and will stop any ordinary attack on it.

facts.text: Brandon's magic sword, which Father William says is needed to kill the dragon, could let the party slay it if retrieved (see thread_11).

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: retrieve the sword (thread_11). Benefit: a weapon said to be able to kill the dragon whose scales nothing else pierces.
classification.support_basis: Would overcome the central obstacle of the unpierceable scales, though it rests on legend and George says no one knows what is true.
classification.action_basis: Father William says the sword is buried with Brandon in the Barrow, and the party is walking there.

facts.resource_subject: Brandon's magic sword needed to kill the dragon

facts.text: Warwick's mithril chain shirt, which Dunk plans to get, could protect against the dragon (see thread_9).

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: obtain the shirt via Dunk's plan (thread_9). Benefit: magical armour for a fighter facing a dragon with a lethal bite.
classification.support_basis: Magical mithril armour reduces the risk of the dragon's bite, though whether it stops poisoned jaws is unknown.
classification.action_basis: Dunk has seen the shirt and has a plan under way to get it.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi's lance; George says a lance may be one of the few weapons not yet tried against the dragon.

classification.support_basis: An untried weapon offers a slim chance against the scales, but George doubts it and nothing has pierced them.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi vowed to George to bring his lance against the dragon, in return for George's help.

classification.stake_basis: George wants the dragon dead but only allowed a lance might be untried and doubted Phidipaldi could kill it; he has no claim on the lance specifically, and killing the dragon any other way would satisfy him.

facts.text: Does Eric the Reeve actually have the 1000 gold he promised for the dragon?

classification.question_basis: George openly doubts Eric has the money; this is a bounded practical check on the reward, not a hidden-story question.
classification.grounding_justification: George's explicit doubt clearly raises it.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A simple fact about Eric's funds.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Asking Eric or townsfolk would likely settle it.

facts.text: Reginald the frog says a little trickster creature called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.
facts.ended_how: no longer relevant: the Clurichen, Naggeneen, was caught and now hangs in a bag behind Quinn's bar

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Reginald only said it was up to no good and to stay away; no specific harm or endangered subject was identified.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: It was described as a little trickster, suggesting mischief rather than grave harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The warning rested on one local creature's testimony, not direct observation by the party.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald described a nightly pattern of it entering town.
classification.preventability_justification: The party was in town at night and could avoid or confront it, but no specific means was established.

facts.text: What is the Clurichen doing in town each night?
facts.ended_how: answered: Naggeneen sneaks into Quinn's basement to drink his ale

classification.question_basis: Reginald said the Clurichen comes into town nightly up to no good without saying what it does; this was a hidden activity worth discovering, not tied to an adventure want.
classification.grounding_justification: Reginald's warning clearly raised that the creature does something unspecified in town each night.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the creature's hidden nightly activity and intention.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning what the trickster does was mildly interesting but not a major revelation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could watch the riverbanks or town at night and follow the creature.

facts.text: Naggeneen the Clurichen, captured in a bag hanging behind Quinn's bar, offers his pot of gold or a secret to whoever releases him; Sir Phidipaldi refused.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: release Naggeneen from Quinn's bag. Benefit: a pot of gold or an unspecified secret, neither linked by play to any want or debt.
classification.support_basis: No established want or debt is served by the gold or the unnamed secret, and releasing him would cross Quinn, who now holds him.
classification.action_basis: Naggeneen did offer the exchange, but no want or debt it would advance is established.

facts.resource_subject: Naggeneen captured in a bag behind Quinn's bar

facts.text: What happened to Bentley's restocking shipment, a week overdue, and why has nothing come into Brandonsford in months?

classification.question_basis: Bentley says his shipment never arrived and nothing like this has happened in centuries, Gill says nothing has come into town in months, and this Session shipments still had not come in. The cause of a town-wide supply stoppage is a hidden circumstance worth discovering, not a routine gap, and no party adventure want is tied to it.
classification.grounding_justification: Two townsfolk reported the stoppage as unprecedented, and the narration again notes shipments still have not come in, keeping the unexplained cause conspicuous.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause cutting off supplies to the whole town, not a simple fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning why the town has been cut off would explain the town's hardship and could change the party's understanding of its troubles.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could question merchants and townsfolk or follow the supply route to trace where shipments stop.

facts.text: With no shipments reaching Brandonsford, the town's supplies are running short; Bentley says the missing shipment is hurting the whole town, and Gill says Warwick the smith has little left to sell.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Bentley and Gill describe a specific harm: the tavern cannot restock and shops have little to sell, hurting the town.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: The harm described is economic hardship and shortage, not established danger to life.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Two townsfolk independently report the shortage, but its extent is only described by them.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Nothing has arrived for months and shipments still have not come in, an ongoing pattern, though no worsening is described.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could look into the missing shipment, but since the cause is unknown the means are uncertain.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned offers himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, doing anything as long as he gets to kill people with the wasp; Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: paying Ned 100 gold a week to hire him. Benefit: an extra killer and his wasp, which he uses to kill things fast, added to the party's fighting strength against the dragon the Reeve wants killed.
classification.support_basis: Ned adds a willing killer and a fast-killing wasp to a dragon hunt, though nothing established shows the wasp works on a dragon and his condition is killing people.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered his and the wasp's services for 100 gold a week, and Uriah is weighing it.

facts.text: Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus.

Farmer Gill offers Dunk his mule Shamus for 100 gold, or in trade for work such as killing the dragon outside town; he says he would go lower than that, though not yet, and has not agreed to Dunk's offer of 20 gold.

classification.opening_basis: The trigger is paying Gill's price or doing the work he names; the benefit is simply obtaining the mule, which is the want itself, so the action pays the item's own price.
classification.support_basis: Meeting Gill's price would get Dunk the mule outright; it adds no separate advantage beyond achieving the want.
classification.action_basis: Gill offered the mule for 100 gold or work in trade, and this Session said he would accept a lower price later.

facts.text: Farmer Gill won't lower the mule's price until his sons, away after the dragon, come back, since he can get no work done without them or a mule.

classification.scope_basis: Gill ties any price drop to his sons' return, which lasts as long as they are away hunting the dragon.

facts.text: Catch whoever empties Quinn's good ale stock at the Golden Egg each night and collect Quinn's 100 gold.
facts.ended_how: achieved: the thief Naggeneen was caught and handed to Quinn, who paid Sir Phidipaldi, Trout and Dr. Uriah 33 gold each

facts.text: Quinn and Sir Phidipaldi have planned a fake ale delivery: Quinn brings bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering ale to the Golden Egg to see who comes for it.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the thief was caught in the basement with marbles and ink before the fake delivery was needed

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: staging the showy fake delivery. Benefit: it baits the nightly thief into revealing themselves without risking real stock, which Quinn proposed for exactly this purpose.
classification.support_basis: It gives the party a concrete way to draw out and observe whoever takes Quinn's ale, though it is untested whether the thief will take the bait.
classification.action_basis: Quinn proposed the sting and agreed to supply bottles; Sir Phidipaldi agreed to perform the delivery.

facts.text: Who or what empties Quinn's good ale each night, leaving half the glasses empty or knocked over? Quinn believes it is Bentley.
facts.ended_how: answered: the thief is the invisible Clurichen Naggeneen, not Bentley

classification.question_basis: Quinn reports his stock vanishing nightly with glasses emptied or knocked over and accuses Bentley only on the basis of Bentley's brew being popular; the culprit is the hidden truth the sting aims to expose. Identifying it is the core of the side job, not an adventure-level end, so it is framed as a revelation.
classification.grounding_justification: Quinn explicitly describes the recurring nightly loss and offers an unproven suspect, making the culprit conspicuously unresolved.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer reveals a hidden nightly actor and their motive, and may overturn Quinn's accusation of Bentley.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning the true culprit would explain the mystery and change how the party sees Bentley or Quinn.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It supports staking out the tavern, the planned sting and questioning townsfolk.

facts.text: Under Trout's Halfling Corps terms, Squints gets second pick of the first treasure, after the elite members, in return for funding himself until then, fighting monsters and taking Trout's orders.

classification.stake_basis: Squints joined looking for his big break and agreed to fund himself and serve under Trout on the promise of this share of the first treasure.

facts.text: Squints, a halfling more experienced at fighting than Trout and armed with a sling and dagger, has joined the party as Trout's junior assistant and takes his orders.

classification.support_basis: An extra experienced fighter and scout who already proved useful at the giant's cottage adds strength for the trip to the Barrow and the dangers ahead.

facts.text: Trout privately told the others they would not rescue Squints if he got caught, so Squints may be left to his fate when he takes risks on Trout's orders.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Trout's whispered plan names a specific endangered subject, Squints, who would be abandoned when in danger.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Being abandoned to a monster could mean serious injury or death for one person.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Trout's own statement to the party establishes the intent, though it was made for one scouting mission.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Trout keeps sending Squints into danger first, but no further abandonment is planned beyond the giant's cottage episode.
classification.preventability_justification: The party controls whether to back Squints up, so it can simply choose to protect him.

facts.text: Get Warwick the smith's magical mithril chain shirt.
Dunk says Warwick's mithril chain shirt could help against the Brandonsford dragon once he has it.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: achieving the want to get the shirt; benefit: magical armor protection when facing the dragon, as Dunk told the party.
classification.support_basis: Magical mithril armor could offer some protection against a dragon whose bite and sulfur have killed many, though how much it would help is unestablished.
classification.action_basis: The shirt is established in Warwick's shop and Dunk stated it could help against the dragon; armor protecting a wearer is a straightforward capability-to-need match.

facts.text: Warwick sleeps in a second-story bedroom whose window is left cracked open, giving a way into his shop-home where the mithril shirt is kept.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: entering through the cracked-open second-story window; benefit: access into the closed shop-home holding the shirt without unlocking the door.
classification.support_basis: It gives physical entry to the house while the shop is closed, though the window opens into the room where Warwick sleeps.
classification.action_basis: Dunk observed the open window; it is a supported physical opening, and Ingrid already climbs to it nightly.

facts.text: Ingrid's sleeping potion for Warwick, being made under Dunk's deal with her, could keep Warwick asleep while Dunk is inside his house.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: carrying out the sleeping-potion plan with Ingrid; benefit: Warwick stays asleep so Dunk can be in the house without waking him.
classification.support_basis: A drugged Warwick removes the risk of the owner waking while Dunk reaches the shirt; the potion is not yet finished.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to make the potion and is working on it; Dunk's plan to get the shirt rests on getting inside while Warwick sleeps.

facts.text: What magic does Warwick's mithril chain shirt have?

classification.question_basis: The shirt glows in moonlight and is clearly magical, but its properties were not described; this is an item-property gap.
classification.grounding_justification: The glow establishes magic but nobody framed its nature as a mystery.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Examining or using the shirt would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental information about an item.

facts.text: Dunk has promised Ingrid that, once she brews the sleeping potion, he will help her get into Warwick's house and give it to Warwick so she can watch him without fear of his waking.

classification.stake_basis: Ingrid is brewing the potion on Dunk's proposal and is relying on him, the tall one, to get her inside, since her greatest fear is Warwick waking and discovering her.

facts.text: Ingrid is brewing a sleeping potion from the faun wine Dunk gave her and expects him tonight; drugging Warwick during the visit would let Dunk into the house while Warwick sleeps, where the mithril chain shirt is kept.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: meeting Ingrid tonight, collecting the potion and dosing Warwick. Benefit: Warwick stays asleep while Dunk is inside his house with the chain shirt, which Dunk told the party is his plan to get it.
classification.support_basis: It gives safe access to the house holding the armour, though Dunk heavily diluted the key ingredient, so the potion may be weak.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to make the potion, accepted the wine and arranged for Dunk to return; Dunk is to help her get it inside.

facts.text: Can Ingrid really make her own potions, as she says, or is Father William right that she cannot?

classification.question_basis: Father William claims Ingrid is incompetent and cannot make her potions herself, while Ingrid says she makes all her products herself; the contradiction bears on whether the sleeping potion will be made at all.
classification.grounding_justification: Two sources make directly contradictory claims.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: It would mostly settle a fact about her skill, though it may touch her ties to the witch Vivian.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: It is mainly useful for whether the plan works.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Watching her work or seeing whether the potion appears would answer it.

facts.resource_subject: Ingrid's ability to make her own potions

facts.text: Will a sleeping potion brewed from Dunk's heavily diluted faun wine still work?

classification.question_basis: Dunk gave Ingrid only about 20% faun wine mixed with tavern wine, so the potion's strength is in doubt; this is a practical item-property gap.
classification.grounding_justification: The deliberate dilution raises the doubt clearly.

facts.text: Ingrid says she owes Dunk for keeping her secret love of Warwick, though Dunk hinted he has not kept it yet, and she fears Warwick learning it.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: calling in Ingrid's acknowledged debt. No specific advantage toward an established want is named.
classification.support_basis: A favour from an alchemist might help, but play established no specific use.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid said she owes him, but no terms or specific help were offered.

facts.text: Father William says the dragon cannot be killed without the magic sword buried with Sir Brandon in Brandon's Barrow Mound; the party could retrieve it from the Barrow.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: retrieving the sword from Brandon's Barrow Mound. Benefit: per Father William, the sword is the only means of killing the dragon, whose scales nothing else has pierced (George). Evidence: beat_47, beat_57, beat_60.
classification.support_basis: It would overcome the dragon's invulnerability, the central obstacle to killing it, though George says no one knows whether the legend is true or where the sword is.
classification.action_basis: The Barrow is a marked, reachable location and the party has already set out for it to get the sword (beat_53, beat_81).

facts.resource_subject: Brandon's magic sword needed to kill the dragon

facts.text: Father William marked Brandon's Barrow Mound on Dr. Uriah's map; it is roughly a three-mile walk north through the forest, though William first said about a day's walk.

classification.support_basis: Knowing where the Barrow is lets the party reach the sword needed against the dragon.

facts.resource_subject: Location and distance of Brandon's Barrow Mound

facts.text: Is the legend of Brandon's fairy-given sword true, and is the sword really in the Barrow Mound?

classification.question_basis: Father William says the sword is buried with Brandon, while George says the tale is a schoolchildren's fairy story and no one knows what is true or where the sword is. The question is a confirmation of a legend rather than an open investigation, so it is ordinary, tied to the dragon hunt.
classification.grounding_justification: George explicitly frames the truth and location of the sword as unknown, contrasting with William's claim.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering it reveals whether an ancient legend holds, more than a simple fact but settled largely by entering the Barrow.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Confirming or debunking the legend would be mildly revealing but is mainly instrumental to killing the dragon.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Farmer Gill knows the fairytales and the Barrow can be searched, plausibly supporting leads.

facts.text: George says Farmer Gill knows the fairytales about Sir Brandon and the magic sword; the party could ask him.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: asking Farmer Gill about the Brandon fairytales. Benefit: learning what the legend says about the sword, which could help find and use it against the dragon. Evidence: beat_60.
classification.support_basis: Folk tales may add detail about the sword, but their reliability is doubtful.
classification.action_basis: Gill is known to the party and George says he knows the tales; asking is a straightforward action.

facts.text: Father William offers to heal Dr. Uriah if he is injured; Uriah would need to return to the church in Brandonsford.

classification.opening_basis: The trigger is Uriah returning to Father William when injured; the benefit is healing. Play establishes no current injury to Uriah and links the healing to no specific want or debt, so the benefit names no particular advantage toward a pursuit.
classification.support_basis: Free healing could aid recovery from wounds suffered on the party's dangerous pursuits, but Uriah is not injured and no specific want depends on it. William's goodwill toward Uriah, a Dagonite he distrusts, is also uncertain.
classification.action_basis: Father William explicitly offered to heal Uriah if he is injured, so the action of going to him is supported by his offer.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah owes Father William penance at Brandon's Barrow Mound, agreed in return for William marking the Barrow Mound and the witch's home on the party's map.

classification.stake_basis: Father William asked for this penance specifically as his price for marking the map, and Uriah accepted after receiving the markings.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah owes Father William a donation of 10 gold for the Barrow Mound's upkeep, agreed in return for William marking the map.

classification.stake_basis: Father William set the 10 gold donation for the Barrow's upkeep as part of his price for marking the map, and he has already delivered his side.

facts.text: A man-eating giant lives in an oversized stone cottage in the woods north of town, on the party's route toward the Barrow; it captured Brother Dirk to eat in its stew and chased the party after they took him. It is slow and tires quickly in pursuit.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The giant seized a traveller heading to the Barrow and meant to eat him, so being captured and eaten is the specific harm to anyone passing near its cottage.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The party saw Dirk bound in a sack beside the giant's cooking pot, Dirk testified it would eat him, and the giant chased them; whether it will strike again is not shown.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: It has already taken one captive and pursued the party, but nothing shows it hunting them further after it tired.
classification.preventability_justification: The party knows where its cottage is and that it is slow and tires, so it can avoid the cottage or outrun it.

facts.text: Brother Dirk, rescued from the giant, was sent by Father William to get Brandon's sword from the Barrow and kill the dragon; the party could persuade him to continue to the Barrow with them. Trout has assigned him to report to Squints, and Dirk has not agreed.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: persuading Dirk to stay with the party. Benefit: another member on the same mission to retrieve Brandon's sword from the Barrow, though no particular skill or knowledge of his is established.
classification.support_basis: Dirk shares the goal of getting the sword, but play establishes no specific capability or knowledge he adds, and he wants to go home.
classification.action_basis: Dirk has not agreed to join. He said he should go home and gave no reply to Trout's assignment, so his cooperation is not established.

facts.resource_subject: Brother Dirk's intentions and place in the party

facts.text: Brother Dirk says he thinks he should just go home rather than continue to the Barrow.

classification.scope_basis: Dirk's stated wish to go home was left unresolved at the stopping point. He gave no reply to Trout's assignment, so it bears on whether he stays beyond the scene.
